revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Water Parks
revealWordProblem.text: Andrew and his friends want to visit a waterpark, but Andrew must take his younger sister who is 8 years old and can only ride waterslides that are less than 100 feet high. Which waterpark should they visit? Include the heights of the slides at the two parks in your recommendation.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Splash Lagoon's slides are 135 ft, 105 ft, 100 ft, 80 ft, and 75 ft. Only 80 ft and 75 ft are less than 100 ft, so 2 of its 5 slides work for Andrew's sister. Wild Bay Waterpark's slides are 128 ft, 120 ft, 108 ft, and 68 ft. Only 68 ft is less than 100 ft, so just 1 of its 4 slides works for her. Since Splash Lagoon has more slides Andrew's sister is allowed to ride (2 versus 1), Andrew and his friends should visit Splash Lagoon.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
conceptIntro.intro: The mean absolute deviation, or MAD, is the average distance of each value from the mean. It tells you how spread out the data is: a small MAD means the data is close together, and a large MAD means it is spread out. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: MAD = the average of how far each number is from the mean (always a positive distance).

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My data set: 6, 8, 10, 12. First I find the mean: 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 = 36, then 36 ÷ 4 = 9. The mean is 9.
Next I find each deviation (value − mean): 6−9 = −3, 8−9 = −1, 10−9 = 1, 12−9 = 3.
Then I take the absolute value of each (the distance, always positive): 3, 1, 1, 3.
Finally I average those distances: 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 8, then 8 ÷ 4 = 2. So the MAD = 2 points.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: New data set: 9, 10, 11. First, what is the mean? Add the three numbers and divide by 3.
Now find how far each number is from the mean. What is the distance for 9? For 10? For 11?
Add those distances and divide by 3. Is this MAD small or large? What does that tell us about the spread?
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

approaching.stem: The mean of a data set is 15. One value is 11. What is the absolute deviation of that value from the mean?
choiceFeedback: Absolute deviation is always positive—take the absolute value of 11 − 15.
The deviation is negative; absolute deviation is the positive version.
Absolute means positive—what's |11 − 15|?
hints: Absolute deviation asks: how FAR is the value 11 from the mean of 15? A distance is always a positive number.
Subtract: value − mean gives the deviation. Then take the absolute value (drop any negative sign) to get the absolute deviation.
Step 1: set up 11 − 15 (the result will be negative). Step 2 is turning that result into a positive distance.
approaching.stemEs: La media de un conjunto de datos es 15. Uno de los valores es 11. ¿Cuál es la desviación absoluta de ese valor respecto a la media?

approaching.stem: A data set has absolute deviations of 3, 1, 5, 2, 4. What is the MAD?
choiceFeedback: Did you find the largest deviation instead of the average?
Add them all and divide by the count of values, not just sum them.
The largest is 5—is MAD the maximum deviation?
hints: You're given the five absolute deviations already — no subtracting needed. MAD is their average.
MAD = (sum of the absolute deviations) ÷ (how many there are). Count them: there are 5 deviations listed.
Step 1: add 3 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 4. Step 2: divide that total by 5. Don't stop after adding — the sum alone is not the MAD.
approaching.stemEs: Un conjunto de datos tiene desviaciones absolutas de 3, 1, 5, 2 y 4. ¿Cuál es la desviación absoluta media (MAD)?
approaching.explanationEs: Suma de las desviaciones absolutas = 3 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 4 = 15. MAD = 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

approaching.stem: The mean of a data set is 20. A value is 26. What is the absolute deviation?
choiceFeedback: Absolute deviation is positive—what's |26 − 20|?
The deviation is positive; absolute value doesn't change it here.
Absolute means take the positive version—what's |26 − 20|?
hints: Same skill as before: absolute deviation is the distance between the value 26 and the mean 20.
Compute value − mean, then take the absolute value. If the difference is already positive, the absolute value keeps it the same.
Step 1: set up 26 − 20. Step 2: check the sign — a positive difference is already a distance, so you're nearly done.
approaching.stemEs: La media de un conjunto de datos es 20. Uno de los valores es 26. ¿Cuál es la desviación absoluta?

approaching.stem: Team A has MAD = 2.1 points. Team B has MAD = 6.8 points. Which team is more consistent?

Team B — higher MAD means better performance
Both are equally consistent
Cannot tell from MAD alone
approaching.explanation: Lower MAD means less spread — Team A's scores stay closer to their average, making them more consistent.
choiceFeedback: A bigger MAD means scores spread wider, not perform better.
Both have the same mean—but which varies less around it?
MAD tells you consistency—smaller MAD is more consistent.
hints: Consistent means scores stay close to the team's average game after game. MAD measures exactly that closeness.
MAD is the average DISTANCE of scores from the mean. Decide whether a small distance or a large distance means 'more consistent.'
Compare what each number says: scores about 2.1 points from the mean vs about 6.8 points away on a typical night. Which team wanders less?
approaching.stemEs: El equipo A tiene una MAD de 2.1 puntos. El equipo B tiene una MAD de 6.8 puntos. ¿Qué equipo es más consistente?
approaching.explanationEs: Una MAD menor significa menos dispersión: los puntajes del equipo A se mantienen más cerca de su promedio, lo que los hace más consistentes.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: Take the ABSOLUTE value of each deviation before adding, so positives and negatives can't cancel: |−2| = 2, |2| = 2, |0| = 0. MAD = (2 + 2 + 0) ÷ 3 = 4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.33 points.
hints: The deviations −2 and 2 cancel to 0 — that's the warning sign. MAD is never 0 unless every value equals the mean.
The 'A' in MAD stands for ABSOLUTE. Take the absolute value of each deviation first: |−2| = 2.
approaching.explanation: The deviations −2, 2, and 0 were found correctly, but the "Find the MAD" step adds them with their signs, so the −2 and the +2 cancel and force a total of 0. The A in MAD means absolute, so take each distance first: 2, 2, and 0. MAD = (2 + 2 + 0) ÷ 3 = 4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.33 points. A MAD of 0 would mean every score equals 8, which is not true here.
approaching.explanationEs: Las desviaciones −2, 2 y 0 se hallaron bien, pero el paso "Find the MAD" las suma con su signo, así que el −2 y el +2 se cancelan y obligan a un total de 0. La A de MAD significa absoluta, así que toma primero cada distancia: 2, 2 y 0. MAD = (2 + 2 + 0) ÷ 3 = 4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.33 puntos. Un MAD de 0 significaría que todos los puntajes son 8, y aquí no es así.

choices: Runner A — lower MAD means more consistent times
Runner B — higher MAD means faster potential
Either — they have the same average
Neither — MAD doesn't matter for relay races
approaching.explanation: Runner A's MAD of 1.2 means times are usually within 1.2 seconds of 60. Runner B's times vary more widely. For reliability, pick Runner A.
choiceFeedback: Bigger MAD means times vary more, not faster potential.
Same average doesn't tell you consistency—MAD does.
MAD directly measures consistency—use it.
hints: 'Reliable' is the key word — the coach wants times that barely change from race to race, not just a good average.
Both runners average 60 seconds, so the average can't decide this. MAD tells you how much each runner's times swing around 60.
First step: read each MAD as a sentence — a MAD of 1.2 means times usually stay within about 1.2 seconds of 60. Do the same for 5.8, then decide.
approaching.stemEs: Dos corredores tienen el mismo tiempo promedio de 60 segundos. La MAD del corredor A es de 1.2 segundos y la del corredor B es de 5.8 segundos. ¿Qué corredor es más probable que el entrenador elija para una carrera de relevos que necesita un tiempo confiable?
approaching.explanationEs: La MAD de 1.2 del corredor A significa que sus tiempos suelen estar dentro de 1.2 segundos de 60. Los tiempos del corredor B varían mucho más. Para tener confiabilidad, se elige al corredor A.

onLevel.stem: A guard scored 2, 4, 6, 8 points in four scrimmages, so the mean is 5 points. The distances from the mean are 3, 1, 1, 3. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
onLevel.explanation: Add the distances: 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 8. Divide by the 4 games: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. The MAD is 2 points.
choiceFeedback: Check the total before you divide — all four distances go into the sum, including both of the larger ones. Then divide that full total by the number of games.
Mean is 5, not the distances—use the distances for MAD.
Did you divide by the number of values (4)?
onLevel.stemEs: Un base anotó 2, 4, 6 y 8 puntos en cuatro partidos de práctica, así que la media es 5 puntos. Las distancias a la media son 3, 1, 1 y 3. ¿Cuál es la desviación absoluta media (MAD)?
onLevel.explanationEs: Suma las distancias: 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 8. Divide entre los 4 partidos: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. La MAD es 2 puntos.
hints: MAD is the average of the distances from the mean, so it is built from those four distances rather than from the scores themselves.
Add all of the distances together, then divide by how many games there were.
Add 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 to get the total distance, then divide that total by the 4 scrimmages.
hintsEs: La MAD es el promedio de las distancias a la media, así que se construye con esas cuatro distancias y no con los puntajes mismos.
Suma todas las distancias y luego divide entre la cantidad de partidos.
Suma 3 + 1 + 1 + 3 para obtener la distancia total y luego divide ese total entre los 4 partidos de práctica.

onLevel.explanation: A smaller MAD means the scores hug the mean. Shooter A's MAD of 2 is smaller than Shooter B's 6, so Shooter A is more consistent.
choiceFeedback: Bigger MAD means scores spread wider, not closer to average.
Scores would vary more with a bigger MAD, not less.
MAD directly tells you how spread out the data is.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos tiradores promedian 11 puntos por partido. La MAD del tirador A es de 2 puntos y la del tirador B es de 6 puntos. ¿Qué tirador es MÁS consistente?
onLevel.explanationEs: Una MAD menor significa que los puntajes se mantienen cerca de la media. La MAD de 2 del tirador A es menor que la de 6 del tirador B, así que el tirador A es más consistente.
hints: MAD measures spread — how far the scores usually land from the average.
Both shooters have the same mean, so the mean cannot settle this. Compare the MAD values instead.
A MAD of 2 means scores usually sit about 2 points away from 11, while a MAD of 6 means they wander about 6 points away. Decide which of those describes scores that stay close to the average.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — The Deviations That Vanished
onLevel.correctWork: MAD uses the ABSOLUTE value (the distance) of each deviation, so the positives and negatives can't cancel out. |−8| = 8, |−4| = 4, |0| = 0, |4| = 4, |8| = 8. MAD = (8 + 4 + 0 + 4 + 8) ÷ 5 = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 rebounds.
hints: Deviations above and below the mean always add up to 0 — that's why a MAD of 0 should look suspicious here.
The 'A' in MAD stands for ABSOLUTE. Take the absolute value of each deviation before you add them.
onLevel.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Las desviaciones que desaparecieron
onLevel.explanation: The mean of 11 and the deviations −8, −4, 0, 4, 8 are correct, but the "Find the MAD" step adds them with their signs, so every negative cancels a matching positive and the total is forced to 0. Signed deviations always sum to zero, which is exactly why MAD uses distances: 8, 4, 0, 4, 8 total 24, so MAD = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 rebounds.
onLevel.explanationEs: La media de 11 y las desviaciones −8, −4, 0, 4, 8 son correctas, pero el paso "Find the MAD" las suma con su signo, así que cada negativo cancela a un positivo y el total queda forzado a 0. Las desviaciones con signo siempre suman cero, y por eso el MAD usa distancias: 8, 4, 0, 4, 8 suman 24, así que MAD = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 rebotes.

onLevel.title: Find the MAD Error
onLevel.correctWork: You must use absolute values of the deviations: |−10| = 10, |−5| = 5, |0| = 0, |5| = 5, |10| = 10. MAD = (10 + 5 + 0 + 5 + 10) ÷ 5 = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.
hints: MAD stands for Mean ABSOLUTE Deviation. What does 'absolute' mean you need to do?
Take the absolute value of each deviation before adding them: |−10| = 10, |−5| = 5, etc.
onLevel.explanation: The mean of 15 and the deviations −10, −5, 0, 5, 10 are all correct. The "Find MAD" step is where it breaks: adding signed deviations always gives 0, because the values below the mean exactly balance the ones above. Use absolute values instead — 10, 5, 0, 5, 10 — which sum to 30, so MAD = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.
onLevel.explanationEs: La media de 15 y las desviaciones −10, −5, 0, 5, 10 están correctas. El paso "Find MAD" es donde falla: sumar desviaciones con signo siempre da 0, porque los valores por debajo de la media equilibran exactamente a los que están por encima. Usa valores absolutos: 10, 5, 0, 5, 10, que suman 30, así que MAD = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

onLevel.prompt: Two basketball teams both average 75 points per game. Team A's last 5 scores: 73, 76, 74, 77, 75. Team B's last 5 scores: 60, 90, 65, 85, 75. Calculate the MAD for each team and explain which team a coach would prefer if they need predictable scoring.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: Team A's MAD = ___. Team B's MAD = ___. Team A is ___ because ___. A coach would prefer Team ___ for predictable scoring because ___.
onLevel.hint: First, find the mean of each team's scores—then calculate how far each score is from mean.
hints: Both teams average exactly 75 points, so the mean can't separate them — the spread (MAD) will.
For each team: find how far each of the 5 scores is from 75 (drop negative signs), add those five distances, then divide by 5. That's the MAD.
Team A first: the distances from 75 are |73−75|, |76−75|, |74−75|, |77−75|, |75−75|. Add them, divide by 5, then repeat for Team B.
onLevel.explanation: Both teams average 75, so the mean cannot tell them apart — the MAD can. Team A's distances from 75 are 2, 1, 1, 2, 0, which total 6, so its MAD is 6 ÷ 5 = 1.2. Team B's distances are 15, 15, 10, 10, 0, which total 50, so its MAD is 50 ÷ 5 = 10. A coach who needs predictable scoring would choose Team A, because a MAD of 1.2 means its scores stay within about a point or two of 75 every game.
onLevel.explanationEs: Los dos equipos promedian 75, así que la media no los distingue: el MAD sí. Las distancias del equipo A respecto a 75 son 2, 1, 1, 2, 0, que suman 6, así que su MAD es 6 ÷ 5 = 1.2. Las distancias del equipo B son 15, 15, 10, 10, 0, que suman 50, así que su MAD es 50 ÷ 5 = 10. Un entrenador que necesita anotación predecible elegiría al equipo A, porque un MAD de 1.2 significa que sus puntajes se mantienen a uno o dos puntos de 75 en cada partido.

onLevel.instructions: The mean is 10. Place each data value on the number line, then find how far each is from the mean: Data: 7, 10, 13.
hints: 7 is 3 units below the mean. 10 is exactly at the mean. 13 is 3 units above the mean.
Absolute deviations: 3, 0, 3. MAD = (3+0+3) ÷ 3 = 2.
onLevel.explanation: With the mean at 10, the distance of each value is what you count on the line: 7 sits 3 ticks below, 10 sits right on the mean for a distance of 0, and 13 sits 3 ticks above. Distance never carries a sign, so the absolute deviations are 3, 0, and 3, and their average is (3 + 0 + 3) ÷ 3 = 2.
onLevel.explanationEs: Con la media en 10, la distancia de cada valor es lo que cuentas en la recta: 7 queda 3 marcas por debajo, 10 cae justo en la media con una distancia de 0, y 13 queda 3 marcas por encima. La distancia nunca lleva signo, así que las desviaciones absolutas son 3, 0 y 3, y su promedio es (3 + 0 + 3) ÷ 3 = 2.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Mean Absolute Deviation is adding the signed deviations (value − mean) instead of their absolute values, so the positives and negatives cancel out to 0. For 6, 8, 10, 12 (mean = 9), the deviations are −3, −1, 1, 3 — they sum to 0, but that is NOT the MAD. Before averaging, take the absolute value of every deviation so each becomes a positive distance: |−3| = 3, |−1| = 1, |1| = 1, |3| = 3. Sum = 8, so MAD = 8 ÷ 4 = 2. A MAD of exactly 0 is a warning sign — it only happens if every value in the data set equals the mean.

check.explanation: Both keepers allowed 10 goals in 6 games: 10 ÷ 6 ≈ 1.67 goals per game.

check.stem: What does a smaller MAD tell you?
choices: The values stay closer to the mean — the keeper is more consistent
The keeper allowed fewer goals overall
The keeper played fewer games
The mean is wrong
check.explanation: MAD is the mean absolute deviation — the average distance from the mean. A smaller MAD means the game-to-game results cluster tightly around that average.

check.stem: Which keeper should the coach start, and why?
choices: Keeper A, because the smaller MAD (0.67) means more consistent performance
Keeper B, because two shutouts is best
Either one, because the means are equal
Keeper B, because a larger MAD means more skill
check.explanation: The means are identical, so the tiebreaker is spread. Keeper A's MAD of 0.67 means most games land near 1.67 goals. Keeper B swings from shutouts to 4-goal games — riskier when one bad game ends the season.

connect.modelAnswer: Both keepers have a mean of about 1.67 goals allowed. The difference is spread: Keeper A's MAD is about 0.67, so their games stay close to that average, while Keeper B's MAD is about 1.33 — twice as variable, swinging between shutouts and 4-goal games. The coach should start Keeper A, because consistency is more reliable when one bad game ends the season.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Data set: 4, 8, 6, 10, 2. The mean is 6. What is the MAD?
choiceFeedback: 6 is the mean — MAD averages the DISTANCES from the mean.
Distances aren't all zero — find each value's gap from 6.
That's the total distance — divide by how many values there are.
hints: The mean (6) is given — your job is to measure how far each of the five values sits from 6.
Plan: find each value's distance from 6 (ignore negative signs), add the five distances, then divide by 5. MAD is that average distance.
First two distances: |4 − 6| = 2 and |8 − 6| = 2. Find the last three the same way, add all five, and divide by 5.
